GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2017-03-07T15:24:19Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: Pipe log to GoAccess not working in cronjob without hyphen
Description: **In Cronjob:**
In version 1.1.1 the following call worked in cronjob:
`zgrep -h '\[07/Mar/2017' /var/log/apache2/access.log.gz |  goaccess --no-progress -q > /path/to/file.html`

In version 1.2 this call works only when I insert a hyphen to goaccess:
`zgrep -h '\[07/Mar/2017' /var/log/apache2/access.log.gz |  goaccess - --no-progress -q > /path/to/file.html`
If the hyphen is not used, I get the help output (goaccess without args)

**Terminal**
In bash terminal both variants work well

Thanks

The problem and solution are clearly described: adding a hyphen character ("-") to the GoAccess command when used in a cronjob. This is a usage/syntax issue that can be verified through code analysis without needing to build or run the software. The issue is about understanding the difference in how stdin is handled in different contexts (cronjob vs terminal), and the solution is simply adding the hyphen parameter to explicitly indicate reading from stdin.
